note: INITIAL AUTHORING (Addendum 02 sections 8-9, spec sections 9-10). Effects are typed modifiers of inputs the Unity vehicle simulation implements (see Core.Builds.SimParam). Numbers are design targets to be calibrated with the Unity handling harness and real driving; nothing here is measured. Prices sit inside the spec section 10 tier ranges; shop availability is by act, never by spending.

chassis.note: Low bonnet line: no room for a supercharger (the turbo kit fits).

parts.name: Street performance tyres
parts.tradeoff: More dry grip than stock; breaks away slightly sooner and a little more sharply.

parts.name: Progressive touring tyres
parts.tradeoff: Smallest peak-grip gain; very progressive breakaway that is easy to catch on damp roads. Wet grip itself is not a separate simulation input yet.

parts.name: Sport compound tyres
parts.tradeoff: Clearly more grip and a sharper turn-in; less warning before the slide and less grip once sliding.

parts.name: Drift compound tyres
parts.tradeoff: Keeps more grip at large slip angles so a slide is easier to hold; lower peak grip and the rear steps out earlier than on sport tyres.

parts.name: Semi-slick tyres
parts.tradeoff: Very high dry grip; a narrow, sudden limit that punishes an untidy entry.

parts.name: Rain-sport tyres
parts.tradeoff: Strong grip with a long, progressive limit for damp and mixed surfaces; less peak grip than semi-slicks.

parts.name: Competition tyres
parts.tradeoff: Highest grip in the catalogue; the least forgiving breakaway and the smallest window to recover.

parts.name: Lowering springs
parts.tradeoff: Lower (20 mm) and firmer: quicker response and less roll; less travel, so kerbs and crests unsettle it sooner.

parts.name: Adjustable sport damper kit
parts.tradeoff: Adjustable springs, dampers, anti-roll bars and ride height (0 to -30 mm). Stiffer and lower sharpens response but costs travel and compliance over kerbs and crests.

parts.name: Rally-spec suspension
parts.tradeoff: Raised (up to +25 mm) and compliant: settles over crests and rough kerbs; the higher centre of gravity rolls more and responds more slowly.

parts.name: Adjustable coilovers
parts.tradeoff: Wide adjustment of springs, dampers, bars and ride height (-40 to +10 mm): the same response-versus-compliance tradeoff with more room to get it right or wrong.

parts.name: Remote-reservoir race suspension
parts.tradeoff: Stiffest range and lightest hardware; very sharp on smooth roads, busy and nervous over rough surfaces unless softened.

parts.name: Street clutch LSD (RWD)
parts.tradeoff: The rear axle breaks away together under power: easier to rotate and hold a slide on throttle; less forgiving if you add power mid-slide.

parts.name: Helical LSD (FWD)
parts.tradeoff: Driven front tyres keep more side grip under power: less power understeer on exits. The corner-entry cost of a locked diff is not simulated yet.

parts.name: Rear-biased viscous centre (AWD)
parts.tradeoff: More torque to the rear: freer rotation on exit; a little less straight-line composure out of slow corners.

parts.name: Adjustable clutch LSD (RWD)
parts.tradeoff: Lock 0-100%: more lock gives stronger throttle rotation and slide hold, less stability when power goes on mid-corner.

parts.name: Adjustable plate LSD (FWD)
parts.tradeoff: Lock 0-100%: more lock gives less power understeer on exits (the entry cost is not simulated yet); 3 kg heavier.

parts.name: Adjustable centre coupling (AWD)
parts.tradeoff: Front torque share 30-50% and lock: rear-biased rotates more freely, front-biased is calmer but pushes wide.

parts.name: Race differential (RWD)
parts.tradeoff: Widest lock range: from very stable to very throttle-steerable; the aggressive end is hard to control.

parts.name: Race differential (FWD)
parts.tradeoff: Widest lock range for exits under power (the entry cost is not simulated yet).

parts.name: Active centre differential (AWD)
parts.tradeoff: Front share 25-50% and lock: the most rotation an AWD chassis can have, or the most stability; not both.

parts.name: Short final drive (fixed)
parts.tradeoff: 6% shorter overall gearing: stronger acceleration in every gear; about 6% less reachable top speed and more shifts.

parts.name: Final-drive kit (adjustable)
parts.tradeoff: Choose the final drive (-8% to +12%): shorter accelerates harder but reaches less top speed; longer does the reverse.

parts.name: Close-ratio gearset
parts.tradeoff: Closer ratios keep the engine near peak power after each shift; a taller first gear launches more softly. Adjustable spread and final drive; slightly quicker shifts.

parts.name: Close-ratio six-speed conversion
parts.tradeoff: Adds a sixth gear for smaller rev drops; 8 kg heavier and one more shift on every straight.

parts.name: Sequential gearbox
parts.tradeoff: Much quicker shifts and at least six gears; 5 kg heavier than stock. Adjustable spread and final drive.

parts.name: Dog-ring race gearbox
parts.tradeoff: Fastest shifts and the widest ratio adjustment; unforgiving to set up, and wrong ratios cost more than they gain.

parts.name: Cold-air intake and map
parts.tradeoff: Stronger low and mid-range pull with a small top-end gain; the alternative to the exhaust in this slot.

parts.name: Free-flow exhaust
parts.tradeoff: More top-end power and 3 kg lighter; slightly softer low-rpm torque than stock.

parts.name: Street breathing package (intake, exhaust, cams)
parts.tradeoff: Clear power gain; the torque peak moves 300 rpm higher, so pull below mid-range feels relatively softer.

parts.name: Street-port rotor housings
parts.tradeoff: More top-end and 400 rpm more revs; little extra torque, so it wants high revs.

parts.name: Forged high-rev internals (inline-4)
parts.tradeoff: Much more top-end and 700 rpm more revs; the torque plateau moves up, so steep climbs need shorter gearing.

parts.name: Stroker torque build (inline-4)
parts.tradeoff: Big mid-range torque for hairpin exits and climbs; a 300 rpm lower rev ceiling and 4 kg heavier.

parts.name: Forged high-rev internals (six)
parts.tradeoff: More top-end and 600 rpm more revs; peakier delivery that needs the right ratios.

parts.name: Stroker torque build (six)
parts.tradeoff: Strong low and mid-range torque; a 300 rpm lower ceiling and 6 kg heavier.

parts.name: Forged high-rev internals (triple)
parts.tradeoff: More top-end and 600 rpm more revs; the small engine gets peakier.

parts.name: Bridge-port rotor housings
parts.tradeoff: Very strong top end and 800 rpm more revs; weak below mid-range, demands high revs and short ratios.

parts.name: Full race engine (inline-4)
parts.tradeoff: Maximum power and 900 rpm more revs; the narrowest useful rev band of any inline-4 option.

parts.name: Full race engine (six)
parts.tradeoff: Maximum power and 800 rpm more revs; peaky delivery that rewards precise gearing.

parts.name: Full race engine (triple)
parts.tradeoff: Maximum power and 800 rpm more revs from the triple; peaky and demanding.

parts.name: Peripheral-port rotor housings
parts.tradeoff: Enormous top end and 1,000 rpm more revs; almost nothing below mid-range.

parts.name: Boost controller and intercooler
parts.tradeoff: More boost: more power and torque, with slightly slower spool-up.

parts.name: Twin-scroll response turbo
parts.tradeoff: 30% quicker spool for sharper exits; only a small peak-power gain.

parts.name: Big-frame turbo
parts.tradeoff: Much more peak power and torque; 40% more lag, so boost arrives late and can unbalance a corner exit.

parts.name: Hybrid race turbo
parts.tradeoff: Maximum boosted power with 20% more lag than stock; 8 kg heavier.

parts.name: Supercharger kit
parts.tradeoff: Instant extra torque with no lag; 16 kg over the nose shifts balance forward. Naturally aspirated front-engine cars only.

parts.name: Turbo conversion kit
parts.tradeoff: Large power and torque gain, but the car becomes turbocharged: 0.75 s spool lag and 22 kg more over the nose. Naturally aspirated front-engine cars only; the NA route stays lighter and instant.

parts.name: Performance pads and fluid
parts.tradeoff: More bite for the same pedal. Braking is still limited by tyre grip; with ABS off the wheels lock sooner.

parts.name: Big brake kit (adjustable bias)
parts.tradeoff: Stronger brakes with adjustable front/rear bias and pressure; 4 kg heavier. Rear bias helps rotation on entry but destabilises trail braking.

parts.name: Race calipers and rotors
parts.tradeoff: Strong, adjustable race brakes; only useful once the tyres can use the force.

parts.name: Carbon-ceramic race brakes
parts.tradeoff: Strongest and 6 kg lighter; a very sharp initial bite that needs a gentle release.

parts.name: Interior strip-out
parts.tradeoff: Removes 35% of this chassis's weight-reduction allowance from the rear cabin: quicker in every direction, balance shifts slightly forward, a little more nervous.

parts.name: Lightweight panels and glass
parts.tradeoff: Removes 65% of the allowance with little balance change; lower yaw inertia makes the car rotate faster and settle less easily.

parts.name: Carbon weight programme
parts.tradeoff: Removes 90% of the allowance, mostly from the nose: sharper and lighter, clearly less stable at the limit.

parts.name: Wide-arch body kit
parts.tradeoff: Wider track (+40 mm) for roll stability and front bite; more drag and 8 kg. Changes the car's silhouette.

parts.name: Carbon body panels
parts.tradeoff: Carbon bonnet, boot and doors: less mass and yaw inertia (quicker, less stable). Counts toward this chassis's weight-reduction limit. Visible carbon finish.

parts.name: Front lip splitter
parts.tradeoff: A little front downforce: sharper high-speed turn-in; slightly more drag and a more front-biased aero balance.

parts.name: Low-drag undertray and mirrors
parts.tradeoff: Less drag for more reachable speed; less downforce, so fast corners feel lighter.

parts.name: Rear spoiler
parts.tradeoff: Rear downforce for high-speed stability; more drag and a rear-biased balance that dulls turn-in.

parts.name: Roof wing
parts.tradeoff: Rear downforce on wagon and hatch roofs; more drag and a rear-biased balance.

parts.name: Adjustable wing and splitter
parts.tradeoff: Substantial adjustable downforce and balance; every step of wing angle trades grip against drag.

parts.name: Adjustable roof wing and splitter
parts.tradeoff: Adjustable downforce and balance shaped for a long roof; the same grip-versus-drag trade.

parts.name: Full aero package
parts.tradeoff: Splitter, wing and diffuser: the most downforce available, with the most drag; wide balance adjustment.

parts.name: Sponsor decal set (+4% event pay)
parts.tradeoff: +4% on ordinary event pay only; never first-clear bonuses, challenge cash, raw drift score, PI or RP. Occupies the single utility slot.

parts.name: Works sponsor package (+8% event pay)
parts.tradeoff: +8% on ordinary event pay only (the cap); never bonuses, raw score, PI or RP. Occupies the single utility slot.

parts.name: Showcase light kit (+5% showcase score)
parts.tradeoff: +5% SHOWCASE drift score only; raw score, qualification, challenges, records and RP never change. Occupies the single utility slot.

parts.name: Showcase stage kit (+10% showcase score)
parts.tradeoff: +10% SHOWCASE drift score only (the cap); raw score and RP never change. Occupies the single utility slot.
